headline: Six courses and a splash: Excitebike gets its NES menu
lede: The arcade's throttle-cooker now opens the way the 1985 cartridge did — pick your circuit from a roster of six before the gate drops. Four new hand-carved tracks, a cursor you can walk with arrows or thumbs, and the two original circuits byte-pinned so no menu PR can ever reshape them.

notes.text: EXCITEBIKE #2563 shipped: marquee → splash → race. SAND CROSS, SLALOM CROSS, BIG AIR and K.O. CROSS join MOTOCROSS and SUPERCROSS; digits 1-6 fast-seat, G sets gear on the splash, Esc steps back, and the phone pad steers the menu (a tap outside it rides). The proven autopilot demo keeps rolling behind the dim.

excitecheck grew a SPLASH block and grew up: terrain, WOT, campaign, determinism and the slack rule now grade ALL SIX courses (autopilot clears every new one in first), and the shipped two are pinned by ground fingerprint + auditor step record. 268/268 checks; a hard-wired cursor turns 8 of them red; exciteplay rides the whole flow with real keys and touch (59/59).

Also on the floor this shift: ArenaArchery's duel seats and kill-juice (#2558/#2565), Missile Battle's seat ceremony (#2510), SmashTV roam tune (#2530) — and slot b's target claim on #2558 was correctly refused by the liveness law, so it built the ladder pick instead of duplicating slot a.

Next up: #2573 files Excitebike's polish pass — EDIT TRACK (draw-your-own-course, the splash's other NES half) leads, then sprite cursors and per-course rival lines. The never-dry ladder now points at ArenaArchery again.
